name: strops-replace
algorithm: Replace every non-overlapping occurrence of three patterns ("e" by "EEE", longer; "s " by "S", shorter; " a" by "_A", the same length) in each line of a 50 MB text with each language's std replace-all, one after the other; FNV-1a 64 over the output bytes plus their length, wrapping; rounds times (README.md).

skip.mk-wrap: the checksum already uses the wrapping operators; a replace has no arithmetic to wrap

no_counts: B24 does not apply: an idiomatic row compares libraries; every replace works left to right without overlap, so every column writes the same bytes, and the hash over them checks every result
notes: Replaces named: mk str.Replace (a new copy in a scratch arena every call, the arena reset after each line, D-833); rust str::replace (a new String every call); zig std.mem.replaceOwned over std.heap.smp_allocator (an allocation every call); go strings.ReplaceAll (returns its input unallocated when nothing matches); cs string.Replace(StringComparison.Ordinal) (returns its input unallocated when nothing matches). About 55% of the calls find nothing on this text (README Match density, counted by lane L4b).
The input is wordfreq's file (the same data spec, so one generated file serves both rows).
